ops.title: Test fixtures can isolate git config for themselves and not for the code under test
ops.body:
A test fixture that sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`/`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`
on **its own git children's `cmd.Env`** isolates only itself. The production code
under test spawns its own children through `render.RunCLI*` with plain
`os.Environ()`, so the developer's `~/.gitconfig` reaches the code being tested
while the fixture that built the repo is immune. The fixture looks isolated; the
assertion is not.

Measured in cc-context (2026-08-02) in two builders since deleted:

- `internal/vcs/diffplan_test.go:25-35` — `gitRepo` built the repo through
  `runGit`, whose `isolatedGitEnv()` (`vcs_test.go:435`) set the three
  `GIT_CONFIG_*` vars on `cmd.Env` only. `ResolveDiffPlan` and every `Git*`
  helper spawn with `os.Environ()`. Same shape in `trunk_test.go` and
  `vcs_test.go`, which shared `runGit`.
- `internal/overview/git_test.go:19-32` — this one used `t.Setenv`, which IS
  process-wide, so it did cover the production probes. Its defect was narrower:
  it never isolated `HOME`, and left `PATH` at the developer's, so a
  brew/mise git answered instead of CI's.

**The setting that makes it bite: `core.quotePath=false`.** With it set globally,
`git ls-files` and `git diff --name-status` emit ZWJ, newline and quote paths RAW
even without `-z`. Dropping `-z` from the shared argv builder (`gitrun.go:74`) —
a real injected fault — went RED on a default machine and would have gone GREEN
on that developer's, silently retiring the whole unquotable-name test family
(`TestGitPathsKeepsUnquotableNames`, `TestResolveDiffPlanGitUnquotableNames`,
`TestRenameOrderReversalAgainstLiveGit`). Two more with the same property:
`diff.renames=false` turns every `R100` into an add+delete pair, gutting the
rename coverage; `init.defaultBranch` decides whether `refs/heads/main` exists at
all, which the trunk local-branch rows hinge on.

The fix is process-wide isolation, not per-child: `internal/vcstest`'s
`isolateEnv` (`fixture.go:245-265`) sets HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, the three
`GIT_CONFIG_*` vars, JJ_CONFIG and a brew-free PATH with `t.Setenv`, so children
spawned with `os.Environ()` inherit it. That is also exactly why no test calling
`vcstest.Repo` can use `t.Parallel()` — see the sibling note.

Generalization worth keeping: **an environment-shaped fixture lie is the same
class as a modeled-bytes fixture lie, and is harder to see.** A stale transcript
is visible in the diff; an inherited config is visible nowhere, and it makes the
test agree with the developer's machine rather than with the tool.
